fields.meta_title: Budget Approval Workflow Built on Your Limits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a budget approval workflow that routes annual budgets, capex requests, line transfers, and over-budget spend to the right approver.
fields.h1: Build a Budget Approval Workflow Around Your Spending Limits
fields.hero_description: Get a budget approval workflow that checks each request against your limits and sends it to the approver they call for.
fields.features_heading: What Decides Who Approves a Budget Request
fields.features_subheading: Your budget policy as an app built by Emergent: the limits that add an approver, the balance each request is checked against.
fields.feature_1:
Limits written in plain English

Describe each rule as your controller would say it: capex over $50,000 goes to the CFO. Emergent builds the request form and routing from that, and changes both when you prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Actuals pulled from your ledger

The app connects to any tool with an API, such as QuickBooks or NetSuite. Spend to date syncs in. Each request is then weighed against what its budget line has left today.
fields.feature_3:
Nudges before a request stalls

An approver who has not decided within the window you set gets a reminder in Slack or by email. After a second miss, the request goes to the backup you named for them.
fields.feature_4:
Every decision on one record

Each decision and its comment is saved with its request in a database you own. Who approved the $120,000 packaging line is answered on that request, not in an email thread.
fields.feature_5:
A live view of what is left

The app can show a live dashboard of every budget line, with approved, spent, and open amounts. Department heads can check their own balance before asking for more money.
fields.feature_6:
No seat for each approver

Apps built on Emergent carry no per-approver seats. Adding a plant manager or the CFO to a rule costs no extra license. The free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Budget Requests, Four Different Limits
fields.tab_content_1:
A $105,000 rise waits for a written reason

Field Operations asks for $855,000 for FY2027, $105,000 more than its $750,000 for FY2026. Any budget more than 10% above last year goes to the CFO with a written reason. The app got one from Odalys Kerrigan, the department head. Mattias Oyelaran in finance has signed off, and it waits for the CFO, Ines Haddad.
fields.tab_content_2:
No payback figure, no CFO review

Desmond Achterberg wants a second packaging line for the plant: $120,000, saving $40,000 a year. Capex over $50,000 needs a payback figure on the form before it moves. The app sent his first draft back with that field marked. He added a payback of 3 years, and the request went to the CFO, Ines Haddad.
fields.tab_content_3:
Software gets $18,000 that travel will not spend

Caspian Rowe in Customer Success asks to move $18,000 out of the travel line and into software. Transfers under $25,000 inside one department need only the department head. This one goes to Yuki Brannigan alone. Once she approves, travel drops to $42,000, software rises to $108,000, and finance gets a notice.
fields.tab_content_4:
$9,500 asked, $6,200 left on the line

Teodor Vasko asks for a $9,500 print run with Kestrel Print Co. for a trade show. The events line has $6,200 left, and the app holds any request larger than its line's balance. It sends the budget owner, Lavinia Osei, a direct message: approve the $3,300 over budget, or move money in first.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Budget Approval Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your budget policy into a budget approval workflow that routes every request, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write each limit as a number
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Choose the fields each rule reads
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather last year's budget requests and capex asks in one sheet. Note who approved each one and how many days it waited, and mark any spend that went ahead before approval.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Group the requests into the decisions your finance team makes: new annual budgets, capex, moves between lines, and spend past a line's balance. Each group gets its own rules.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Turn every judgment call into a figure: a large request becomes one over $10,000, and a quick reply becomes 3 working days. A limit with a number in it routes the same way for every department head.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List what the form must ask so the rules can run, such as the budget line, the amount, and the payback in years. A rule that needs a field the form lacks cannot route anything.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Name a backup for each approver
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide how long a request may wait with one person before a reminder goes out, and who takes over after that. The CFO needs a backup too, especially during year-end planning.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste your limits and form fields into Emergent as a short prompt, one rule per line. It turns them into a working app, and you change any rule later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before going live, replay three of last year's requests, one from each of three groups. Each should land with the approvers who decided it then; adjust any rule that sends one somewhere new.

faq_plan.q: What is a budget approval workflow?
faq_plan.a: A budget approval workflow is the set of rules a budget, or a change to it, passes through before money can be spent. The rules say who reviews it, in what order, and which limits add another approver. It covers the annual budget itself and the requests that change it during the year, such as capex and transfers between lines.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a budget approval workflow?
faq_plan.a: Write down the limits that change who approves a budget request, then describe them to Emergent's AI automation builder in plain English. It builds the form and the routing rules, with a record of each decision. Replay a few of last year's requests through it before department heads start submitting new ones.

faq_plan.q: What should a capex approval workflow ask for on the request form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for what the CFO needs to decide without a follow-up email. That means the asset and its cost, the yearly savings it brings, the payback in years, and the budget line it comes from. Require the payback field above your capex limit. An incomplete request then goes back to its owner instead of waiting in the CFO's queue.

faq_plan.q: How is a budget approval workflow different from other approval workflows?
faq_plan.a: It weighs each request against what is left on its budget line, while a time-off or policy request has no balance to check. Keep that balance check in the budget rules, and let a general approval workflow handle the requests that carry no amount.

faq_plan.q: How many approval levels does a budget approval workflow need?
faq_plan.a: As few as the amount calls for: one approver for a small transfer inside a department, more for a new annual budget or a large capex request. Each level you add is one more person the request waits on. Check last year's requests and drop any level whose approver never changed an outcome. The apps Emergent builds have no per-approver seats.

faq_plan.q: Should a budget approval workflow block spend or only warn when a line runs out?
faq_plan.a: Use both, split by amount: hold large overages and warn on small ones. A hold makes the budget owner choose between approving the overage and moving money in from another line. A warning lets the spend go ahead and flags it for the monthly review. Pick the figure, such as $500 over, below which the app only warns.

faq_plan.q: How should a budget approval workflow handle changes after the budget is approved?
faq_plan.a: Treat each change as its own request, and keep the approved budget as a version nobody edits. A mid-year transfer or a reforecast then records what changed and who approved it, with the balance before and after. If the budget lives in a spreadsheet passed around for sign-off, a document approval workflow keeps each version tied to the approvals it received.

faq_plan.q: When should a budget approval workflow send a transfer to finance?
faq_plan.a: Whenever money leaves one department for another, because two budget owners are affected and neither can approve for the other. Route the transfer to both department heads, then to finance. Moves inside one department can stay with its head below a limit you set, with finance getting a notice instead of a request.

faq_plan.q: How long should a budget approval workflow wait before it escalates a request?
faq_plan.a: Pick a window your approvers agree to, such as 2 working days, then pass the request to the backup named for that person. Shorten it near quarter close, when a stalled request can push spend into the next period. The app Emergent builds sends the reminder through Slack or email and escalates when the window closes.

faq_plan.q: Should a budget approval workflow check invoices against the approved budget?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the invoice is charged to a budget line. Have your invoice approval workflow read that line's remaining balance before payment, and send any invoice larger than the balance to the budget owner. Data lives in a database you own, where the budget and the invoices it pays can sit side by side.

plan.angle: The top results explain budget approval as a generic cycle (prepare, review, approve). This page shows the four decisions a budget approval workflow actually routes, as working screens: an annual department budget that rises more than 10% and needs a written reason before the CFO, a capex request over $50,000 that must carry its payback before it moves, a mid-year transfer between two lines of one department, and a spend request larger than what is left on its budget line. Generic routing belongs to the approval workflow page, single invoices to the invoice approval page and receipts to expense report automation; this page stays on approving the budget and changes to it.
